# EXPLAIN ANALYZE evidence (T-27)

_Generated by `npm run docs:explain`. Each experiment adds synthetic rows inside a transaction, times the query without and with the index, then rolls everything back._

## Summary

| Query | Index | Before | After | Speed-up |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q2 overdue open tasks (60,000 tasks, 0.5% open) | idx_tasks_due_open (partial index) | 5.301 ms | 0.235 ms | 22.6x |
| Q11 open feedback per student (60,000 items, 0.4% open) | idx_feedback_assignee_open (partial index) | 5.289 ms | 0.306 ms | 17.3x |
| Q6 five nearest vectors (6,000 vectors, 384 dims) | idx_embeddings_hnsw (HNSW, cosine) | 4.717 ms | 1.975 ms | 2.4x |

Q4 (milestones with unresolved feedback) uses `<>`, which no B-tree index can answer, so it is not index-driven; its joins use the primary-key and `idx_reviews_milestone` indexes. On the real demo data (a few dozen rows per table) PostgreSQL chooses sequential scans whatever indexes exist, which is why the synthetic rows are needed to show the effect.

## 1. Q2: teams with overdue open tasks

Index: `idx_tasks_due_open ON tasks(due_date) WHERE status NOT IN ('done','verified')`. Only open tasks can be overdue, so the partial index is tiny.
